recommendations.rationale: Retained evidence is consistent with several unresolved causes (residual tip speed under weak velocity weighting, solver stop-short, shrinking effective horizon, projected-model mismatch) and does not distinguish them; defer any control-parameter change until the single authorized bounded 0.01 s saved-state check is executed.

attribution.reason: Terminal and late tip speeds greatly exceed the 0.02 m/s settling limit while terminal position is within tolerance; the saved objective weights velocity terms small (velocity_weight 0.0001, terminal_velocity_weight 0.0001, terminal_tip_speed_weight 0.0, holding_tip_speed_weight 0.0) with terminal_weight 5.0. Raw weight magnitudes do not establish cost-term importance without actual contributions/scaling, so this stays unresolved.

34 of 35 selections are 'User_Requested_Stop' against 1 'Solve_Succeeded', with policy_stop_reason 'budget_best_feasible' or 'relative_seed_improvement'; plans were still 'plan_accepted' true. A stop-short category does not by itself establish suboptimality or its link to settling, and no iteration traces are retained.

Effective horizon declines from 8 to 3 control intervals across the sampled late updates (far below the configured horizon of 10). A reduced lookahead could limit braking/terminal-speed shaping, but the retained signals do not separate horizon from solver stops or weighting.

Projected-GVS predictions and recorded serial-backend endpoints differ by small but nonzero world-tip distances and one-step velocity-vector norms. Boxed 0.01 s comparisons cannot establish that this mismatch dominates settling, so it remains a candidate.

35 deadline misses and mean_update_s 17.075238151415917 s versus a 0.01 s control period are recorded, but scheduling is synchronous: controller calls complete before fixed-count backend steps and wall deadline misses do not inject physical delay into simulated time, so a wall-clock mechanism cannot directly cause the physical settling failure.

At update 30 the applied/requested tension on channel 0 is 7.990411884680996 N, close to the 8.0 N per-tendon limit held in source.force_limits; force-limit proximity could bound available braking tension, but the retained signals do not quantify lost authority, so this is unresolved.

facts.statement: Reach passed while sampled settling failed: terminal tip error 0.007642608585867386 m is within the 0.01 m reach tolerance and reach_passed is true, but sampled_settling_passed is false, with late-window max tip error 0.05813810428573256 m against the 0.01 m settling position limit.
Tip speed is far above the settling limit: terminal tip speed 0.6351726092425104 m/s and late-window max speed 1.5810152739742807 m/s both exceed the 0.02 m/s settling_criteria speed limit.

Late-window selections ended short of convergence with shrinking lookahead: effective horizon falls from 8 control intervals at update 27 to 3 at update 32, only 1 of 35 selections reports 'Solve_Succeeded' versus 34 'User_Requested_Stop', and the run logs 35 deadline misses with mean_update_s 17.075238151415917 s against a 0.01 s control period.

Projected-GVS versus recorded-backend comparisons at updates 27 to 29 show small but nonzero world-tip differences of 0.0059230819406683064 m (update 27) and 0.0076898869753466255 m (update 29) and one-step velocity-vector difference norms of 0.021386880777076088 m/s (update 28) and 0.14969247760063253 m/s (update 29).

limitations: No historical optimizer iterations or full warm plans are reconstructed; source.historical_full_plans is not retained.

Projected states are projected GVS coordinates, not full backend-state error.
recommended_actions: Execute at most one authorized bounded saved-state check (prediction_braking and/or local_comparison) at one saved projected state under horizon_s 0.01, integration_step_s 0.002, model.gvs@1.0.0, to measure the local endpoint speed/position difference.
Do not change control parameters based on this phase; keep weighting, solver-stop, horizon, and model-mismatch hypotheses open.
